newsitem.title: USA: Conn. tax chief accuses banks of tax scam -- report.
newsitem.headline: Conn. tax chief accuses banks of tax scam -- report.

text.p: Connecticut Revenue Services Commissioner Gene Gavin accused several state banks of creating a "significant corporate tax scam," Hartford Courant reported Tuesday.
Gavin said the scheme could cost the state up to $50 million a year in lost revenue.
He said he would use his discretionary power to block the tax shelter, which was made possible by a change last year in federal banking law.
Gavin also said he would seek state legislation to permanently block the practice.

"In our view, banks are taking a legitimate tax vehicle and abusing it," the paper quoted Gavin as saying. "They are doing it in such a way that the result was never anticipated by the state of Connecticut."
The practice could penalize corporations that pay their taxes, Gavin said. It could also jeopardize tax-cutting proposals being mulled by the governor and state legislators.
Gavin said the banks are trying to shelter mortgage income from state taxes by transferring their mortgage portfolios to a corporate entity known as a REIT, or real estate investment trust.
Profits paid from a REIT to a bank are not taxed under state law, so a bank theoretically could escape Connecticut taxes on all income from its mortgages in this way.
The paper said Waterbury, Conn.-based American Bank of Connecticut was the only institution in the state to receive permission from banking regulators to place mortgages into a REIT.
Documents filed with state banking officials indicate that American Bank of Connecticut planned to put as much as $260 million in mortgage holdings into a REIT, the paper said.
